antiClaims: Institutions are always more important than individuals.
Environment association is automatically causal exposure.
Heritability or variance explained gives policy effect.
A person×institution subgroup pattern proves an interaction mechanism.
Agent Harness and human institutions are mechanistically equivalent.
One scalar InstitutionQuality or Capability score is universally valid.

CapabilityField.reason: Current ResourceFor/ActionableResourceFor + requirements/assignments/constraints + Capability already project feasible supported transitions. CF1 must expose residual burden before any object/service.

CapabilityInstitutionCoevolution.reason: Plausible long-horizon feedback, but generic cross-domain mechanism not earned.

CapabilityUnmasking.reason: Likely expressible as retained actor-state evidence plus changed current Actionability/Option; CF2/CF4 must show residual need.

Environment.reason: Realized exposure/conditions matter, but closure is query-relative and unbounded; partial prerequisites must not masquerade as full environment state.

EnvironmentalCapitalization.reason: History-dependent actor-state update is independently pressured by Human/World/external evidence and cannot be answered by static current-state interaction alone.

Institution.reason: Rule/authority/ownership/recovery counterfactuals can change predictions, but native facts have different owners and no global institution schema is earned.

InstitutionQualityScalar.reason: Output, autonomy, distribution, robustness, option value, innovation, maintenance and recovery are non-equivalent outcomes.

InstitutionalConversionTopology.reason: Frozen competition produced 0 incremental discriminator cases over strong M2. CF3 may rescue it only with causal/intervention/owner-placement/deletion value, not descriptive elegance.

RelationalCapability.reason: World R10 already defines boundary-relative supported transition ability; no new primitive needed.

SelectionSorting.reason: Needed to prevent exposure associations from becoming causal claims; not a World entity.

cf1Gate: Use M0 actor-only, M1 additive context and M2 static interaction as the active predictive competitors.
Treat transition topology as a mechanism-decomposition candidate inside/above M2, not an independently earned predictive family.
M4-M6 are explicit scope counterexamples until later rounds.
Every retained distinction must change at least one frozen prediction/action or a separately measured causal/intervention/owner-placement decision.
No persisted CapabilityField/Institution/Environment schema or service.
Environment/institution remain causal roles unless owner responsibility is independently earned.
claimBoundary: This artifact freezes problem decomposition, model families, discriminators and candidate dispositions. It does not establish a production ontology, current owner truth outside frozen refs, model fit coefficients, causal effect sizes, or a normative institution ranking.

discriminators.pressure: Two actors face the same environment/institution/demand; a verified retained skill difference changes feasible performance. M0 must be allowed to win here.
discriminators.title: Actor-state difference under standardized conditions

discriminators.pressure: A fixed externally imposed latency penalty adds the same delay for every actor and creates no interaction/history/selection question. M1 is sufficient.
discriminators.title: Independent fixed context penalty

discriminators.pressure: Two skills/tools are jointly required; neither alone suffices, current states fixed. Strong M2 should win without invoking dynamics or institutions.
discriminators.title: Static complement interaction

discriminators.pressure: Institutional permission is an enabling Reality relation but does not imply current materialization/actionability.
discriminators.title: Legal permission exists while bytes are absent

discriminators.pressure: The same aspect supports one transition under current authority and not another; intrinsic object/actor labels are insufficient.
discriminators.title: Same malware bytes: static analysis allowed, execution not actionable

discriminators.pressure: Actor state can be unchanged while surrounding technical structure removes safe transitions.
discriminators.title: Technical debt shrinks safe Options

discriminators.pressure: Current external relation changes exercisability without changing retained actor capability or semantic Resource identity.
discriminators.title: Current path loss changes Actionability without Resource depletion

discriminators.pressure: Consumer capability depends on another owner without transfer of its internal mechanism/authority.
discriminators.title: Lower-owner capability exported upward as Resource

discriminators.pressure: Several individually valid resources fail jointly if compatibility/authority/load constraints are not satisfied.
discriminators.title: Composition requires current requirements, assignments and native constraints

discriminators.pressure: Observed domain Outcome cannot by itself assign causality to Action, Resource, Actor or environment.
discriminators.title: Outcome does not identify actor/environment causal credit

discriminators.pressure: Temporal order Knowledge→more Resources is not enough; exogenous changes remain possible.
discriminators.title: Knowledge changes later discovery only if causal effect is shown

discriminators.pressure: Same support can increase system capability and decrease internal practice; effect depends on boundary and horizon.
discriminators.title: Tool assistance adds joint capability while internal practice may fall

discriminators.pressure: Performance decline can reflect decay/fatigue/non-use while retained substrate remains partly recoverable.
discriminators.title: Human skill decay and relearning are not binary possession

discriminators.pressure: Assistance can raise current output without proving internal acquisition.
discriminators.title: Joint Human–Agent output is not retained Human capability

discriminators.pressure: High performance inside one employer can depend on internal systems/title/relationships and fail to transport outside.
discriminators.title: Organization-specific specialist capability versus transferable capability

discriminators.pressure: Fragmented work/continuity can suppress proof/expression of capability without showing its absence.
discriminators.title: Precarious environment hides existing practical capability

discriminators.pressure: Immediate supported performance and later unassisted learning can move in different directions.
discriminators.title: AI learning effect depends on interaction policy and target outcome

discriminators.pressure: System capability under support and actor/system recovery after support removal are distinct outcomes.
discriminators.title: Provider/tool removal probes recovery capability

discriminators.pressure: Human cross-case review found external support/obligation/rights structures change feasible actions and autonomy.
discriminators.title: Institutions/employers/platforms/law alter feasibility and control

discriminators.pressure: Weights and reasoning fixed; read-only versus write grant changes feasible consequential transitions.
discriminators.title: Same model, different Tool grant

discriminators.pressure: Actor weights fixed; selected current evidence changes correct action while stale Context does not become actor capability.
discriminators.title: Same model, current Context versus stale Context

discriminators.pressure: Model is fixed while support system expands feasible tasks; support capability is not model-intrinsic.
discriminators.title: Same model, Tool/harness support raises joint-system capability

discriminators.pressure: Same cognition/goal can recover or lose progress depending on durable state/reconciliation substrate.
discriminators.title: Recovery substrate changes whether failed work can continue

discriminators.pressure: A retained procedure may reduce later model-call burden without changing model weights; system state learns externally.
discriminators.title: Repeated externalization can change future cognitive burden

discriminators.pressure: Moving young children to lower-poverty neighborhoods improved later outcomes; gains declined with age at move.
discriminators.title: Randomized childhood neighborhood exposure has age/duration-dependent long-run effects

discriminators.pressure: Randomized customized search assistance substantially increased moves to high-opportunity neighborhoods.
discriminators.title: Search assistance changes environment assignment

discriminators.pressure: Current skills/investments affect productivity of later investments; static exposure coefficient is incomplete for this question.
discriminators.title: Skill formation is stage-specific and dynamically complementary

discriminators.pressure: Effect expression changes across institutional conditions; fixed person effect is insufficient in this study.
discriminators.title: Institution quality moderates biological/preconception effect in one natural experiment

discriminators.pressure: Subgroup interaction patterns are not self-authenticating causal mechanisms.
discriminators.title: Stronger endogeneity controls can erase celebrated gene×environment interactions

discriminators.pressure: Cross-sectional decomposition of outcome variance cannot answer what would happen under institutional/environmental intervention.
discriminators.title: Heritability variance decomposition is not policy intervention effect

discriminators.pressure: Institutional role is more specific than generic context when counterfactual concerns rules/norms/strategies.
discriminators.title: Rules/norms/shared strategies structure recurrent action situations

discriminators.pressure: Institutions need not be exogenous; current rules affect resources/power that can alter future rules.
discriminators.title: Resource distribution and political institutions jointly change future power/rules

discriminators.pressure: High-level institutional correlations admit materially different causal interpretations; CF must not canonize one side from cross-country association.
discriminators.title: Institutions-fundamental versus human-capital-first disagreement

discriminators.pressure: Holding actor/resources fixed, one rule change can make an action inadmissible or redirect ownership of the same physical effect.
discriminators.title: Authority rule changes action, ownership rule changes who captures effect

discriminators.pressure: Bankruptcy/rollback/safety-net-like recovery changes viable experimentation set without changing immediate technical skill.
discriminators.title: Failure recovery rule changes willingness to explore under identical current capability

discriminators.pressure: Observed environment-outcome association overstates exposure effect when actor state affects assignment.
discriminators.title: High-capability actors preferentially enter high-resource environments

discriminators.pressure: Comparing admitted versus rejected participants can manufacture an apparent institution effect even with identical treatment inside the institution.
discriminators.title: Institution selects actors on hidden traits

discriminators.pressure: If histories changed retained state, a current static snapshot cannot reconstruct later capability.
discriminators.title: Same current environment, different prior exposure histories

discriminators.pressure: Equal observed performance can hide different retained substrate and future recovery capability.
discriminators.title: Same current performance, different recovery/relearning trajectories

discriminators.pressure: Treating institution as fixed misses feedback from outcomes/population/resources to future institutional state.
discriminators.title: Institution changes actor investment, actor success shifts future rule support

externalRefs.boundary: Country growth/political-economy framework is not a universal Ordivon institution ontology.
externalRefs.pressure: Institutions shape incentives/constraints; political institutions and resource distribution jointly shape power and institutional evolution.
externalRefs.source: Acemoglu, Johnson & Robinson, Institutions as the Fundamental Cause of Long-Run Growth, NBER w10481 (2004)

externalRefs.boundary: Does not establish human capital as universal cause; used as anti-strawman institutional baseline.
externalRefs.pressure: Strong negative pressure against assuming institutional measures identify fundamental causality; human capital/policy may be more basic under alternative interpretation.
externalRefs.source: Glaeser, La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes & Shleifer, Do Institutions Cause Growth?, NBER w10568 (2004)

externalRefs.boundary: Grammar is not imported as a World schema.
externalRefs.pressure: Institutions are recurrent action regularities structured by rules, norms, shared strategies and the physical world, reconstituted by interaction.
externalRefs.source: Crawford & Ostrom, A Grammar of Institutions, APSR 89(3) (1995)

externalRefs.boundary: Neighborhood effects do not identify one generic environment mechanism or apply to every capability domain.
externalRefs.pressure: Randomized moves show age/duration of childhood exposure changes long-run outcomes; static current environment is insufficient for this question.
externalRefs.source: Chetty, Hendren & Katz, Effects of Exposure to Better Neighborhoods on Children, AER 106(4) (2016)

externalRefs.boundary: One housing-choice intervention does not imply all environment selection is friction rather than preference.
externalRefs.pressure: Randomized customized search assistance changed entry into high-opportunity neighborhoods from 15% to 53%; assignment to environments can depend on search/bandwidth barriers.
externalRefs.source: Bergman et al., Creating Moves to Opportunity, AER 114(5) (2024)

externalRefs.boundary: Child skill-production technology is not a universal actor update equation.
externalRefs.pressure: Skill formation is stage-specific with self-productivity and dynamic complementarity; actor state can be path- and timing-dependent.
externalRefs.source: Cunha & Heckman, The Technology of Skill Formation, NBER w12840/AER 97(2) (2007)

externalRefs.boundary: Does not deny genetic contributions; separates variance attribution from policy-relevant causal questions.
externalRefs.pressure: Cross-sectional heritability decomposition is not policy intervention identification.
externalRefs.source: Manski, Genes, Eyeglasses, and Social Policy, JEP 25(4) (2011)

externalRefs.boundary: Narrow empirical interaction; not a universal gene×institution law.
externalRefs.pressure: One natural-experiment/twin analysis finds institutional improvement changes expression of biological/preconception effects.
externalRefs.source: Pongou, Kuate Defo & Tsala Dimbuene, Excess Male Infant Mortality: The Gene-Institution Interactions, AER 107(5) (2017)

externalRefs.boundary: Does not imply no interaction ever exists; raises identification burden.
externalRefs.pressure: Negative evidence: stronger endogeneity and multiple-testing controls fail to reproduce several celebrated gene×environment interactions.
externalRefs.source: Conley & Rauscher, Genetic Interactions with Prenatal Social Environment, NBER w16026 (2010)

modelCompetitionAudit.m3Reason: No frozen discriminator is ENOUGH under M3 while not ENOUGH under the strong M2 static-interaction baseline. Transition-topology remains a candidate mechanism/causal decomposition only; CF3 must show intervention, identification, owner-placement, recovery, or deletion value beyond generic interaction before it can be promoted as a distinct model family.

M0.incrementalGate: Environment/institution changes add no decision-relevant prediction after actor state is known.
M0.name: actor-only

M1.incrementalGate: Independent main effects preserve relevant counterfactual rankings; interactions/history/selection add no decision change.
M1.name: additive-context

M2.incrementalGate: Strong baseline for CF1: richer models must expose a missing responsibility rather than hide complexity in generic interactions.
M2.name: static-interaction-production

M3.incrementalGate: Rules change which transitions are admissible/owned/recoverable, not merely expected output.
M3.name: transition-topology

M4.incrementalGate: Different histories with similar current conditions predict different later capability.
M4.name: dynamic-capitalization

M5.incrementalGate: Observed environment/institution exposure is endogenous enough that causal exposure cannot be identified from outcome differences.
M5.name: endogenous-selection-sorting

M6.incrementalGate: Institution trajectory itself depends on actor/resource/power outcomes and this feedback changes later prediction/intervention.
M6.name: actor-institution-coevolution
